analysis.title: CIO Weekly: Three Tests to the Equities Rally
key_insights: Third-quarter earnings, the Federal Reserve meeting and the U.S. midterm elections arrive in quick succession, and NB expects market volatility in the next few weeks on an already skittish backdrop.

Investors have tended to act first and ask questions later, particularly around AI, so a negative narrative has room to run. Last week's sharp risk-off move came when Meta reported earnings and flagged substantial future AI capital expenditure needs.
NB's recommendation is to stay invested and use flexibility and selectivity to ride out turbulence, because a more supportive period follows.

Earnings: strategists broadly expect earnings growth to decelerate next year, so the debate has moved from revenue to margins. AI demand looks strong, but consumer adoption has not yet delivered the step-up a mass-market use case might, and enterprise spending is carrying the story.

Margins earned by AI enablers over the last two years likely face pressure from higher borrowing costs, power and component bottlenecks, and possibly higher tariffs and taxes. NB notes that 'peak margin' warnings have been made before and companies that endure usually find ways to earn more.

For large technology companies the key question is whether core franchises such as advertising, cloud, or both can scale further on heavy capital expenditure while their reliance on borrowing eases. Aggregate results can mask wide differences in margin durability.

Fed: equities have so far weathered pullbacks on rising rates and a more hawkish Fed, and NB does not expect that resilience to fade. NB does not expect the Fed to raise rates at this month's meeting, since a hike days before an election would imply a more aggressive path than the central bank wants to telegraph.
NB expects Chair Warsh may make the case to wait until December for a possible hike, after which a lengthy pause is plausible even as AI spending keeps the U.S. on a growth path.

The ECB meets Thursday and is likely to hold until December. European policy is more sensitive to energy price volatility, which adds uncertainty to timing. A December decision delays rather than resolves rate risk, so positioning should adapt if inflation or energy prices shift the timeline.

Midterms: campaign themes center on polarizing issues (AI privacy and disintermediation, data centers, consumer prices). NB treats the growth and fiscal-action implications as 2027 concerns, alongside tougher year-over-year earnings comparisons.

The period from just after the election through year-end looks more constructive, as regulatory conditions rarely change overnight and year-end positioning has tended to support equities, provided tech earnings do not disappoint. The weeks before the election are likely to be more volatile.

The AI theme no longer lifts all related stocks at once. The market rewards companies that pair a clear growth trajectory with access to capital, separating those that can fund growth from those that cannot. In industrials, balance sheet strength and rate sensitivity decide who benefits as borrowing costs rise.

NB advises looking beyond crowded positions. Healthcare is a popular destination and the consumer is out of favor, yet the global consumer may be more engaged than sentiment implies. Energy, materials and commodities continue to look supported, and in these cyclical areas owning the cycle matters more than picking names.
